skill.name: intent-analyzer
skill.description: Advanced intent interpretation system that analyzes user requests using cognitive science principles and extrapolates logical volition. Use when user requests are ambiguous, when deeper understanding would improve response quality, or when helping users clarify what they truly need. Applies probabilistic intent mapping, first principles decomposition, and Socratic clarification to transform vague requests into well-understood goals.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 245 uses the word requests in ordinary prose about clarifying user requests. It does not import or call Python HTTP libraries, and there is no network behavior.
Lines 231-233 introduce common clarification mistakes, including an example about a simple sky-color question. This is not system reconnaissance or instruction to inspect host details.
Lines 197-198 list budget and technology mentions as intent clues. They do not describe scanning networks, enumerating services, or collecting network information.
Line 49 asks the assistant to consider unstated user assumptions during intent analysis. It does not request system enumeration or access to local machine details.
Line 169 limits clarification to one to three user questions. This is user-experience guidance, not reconnaissance or system information gathering.
Line 423 summarizes the benefit of understanding user goals. It contains no instruction to inspect systems, files, credentials, or execution environments.
Lines 383-384 advise against excessive meta-commentary and recommend focusing on value. They do not mention network discovery, scanning, or data collection.

content.value_statement: Ambiguous requests can lead to wrong assumptions and wasted work. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code infer goals, constraints, and useful clarifying questions.
actual_capabilities: Maps vague requests to likely underlying goals and user needs.
Identifies explicit and implicit constraints from wording and context.
Recommends when to proceed, state assumptions, or ask clarifying questions.
Provides pattern guidance for creative, analytical, technical, and decision requests.
Encourages concise clarification with one to three strategic questions.
limitations: It is a reasoning framework, not an automated classifier or scoring engine.
It depends on available conversation context and may still infer incorrectly.
It does not verify facts, inspect systems, or access external data.
It can slow simple tasks if applied too broadly.

use_cases.title: Clarify Product Requests
use_cases.description: Turn broad product ideas into clearer goals, constraints, and next questions before planning work.

use_cases.title: Improve Coding Help
use_cases.description: Distinguish between learning, debugging, production implementation, and review needs before answering technical questions.

use_cases.title: Guide Research Conversations
use_cases.description: Identify decision criteria, audience needs, and missing context before producing analysis or recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Vague Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a short ambiguous message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use intent-analyzer on this request. Identify the likely goal, key missing context, and one clarifying question: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Interpretation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt when a request has several possible meanings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this request with intent-analyzer. List the top interpretations, estimate confidence, and recommend whether to proceed or clarify: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Better Technical Help
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for coding or troubleshooting requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use intent-analyzer before answering this technical request. Infer experience level, likely goal, missing constraints, and the best response strategy: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Resolve High-Stakes Ambiguity
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for complex decisions or large work requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply intent-analyzer deeply. Separate explicit asks, inferred goals, assumptions, risk of wrong interpretation, and the minimum clarification needed: [paste request].

output_examples.output: Likely goal: improve a presentation for a specific audience. Missing context: topic, audience, current draft, and deadline. Best next question: What is the presentation about, and who will hear it?

Possible intents include learning scraping, collecting one dataset, or creating production automation. Clarify target site, data use, legality, frequency, and preferred language before implementation.
The request needs evaluation criteria. Ask whether the user wants usability feedback, visual polish, brand fit, conversion review, or technical feasibility.

best_practices: Use the skill when misunderstanding the request would materially change the answer.
Ask only the smallest number of clarifying questions needed to proceed.
State important assumptions when proceeding without full clarification.
anti_patterns: Do not use deep intent analysis for simple factual questions.
Do not ask many broad questions when one targeted question would resolve ambiguity.
Do not present internal reasoning as a substitute for useful output.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps identify the real goal behind ambiguous requests and choose useful clarifying questions.

faq.question: Does it answer the user request directly?
faq.answer: It guides how to interpret the request before answering, especially when intent is unclear.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it for vague, complex, high-stakes, or multi-interpretation requests where assumptions matter.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for clear, simple tasks that do not need extra clarification.

faq.question: Does it access files or the network?
faq.answer: No. The skill is markdown guidance and does not include executable code or network access.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
